verdict.summary: Kani 0.67.0 verifies the ACTUAL shipped ws_core source. 16 harnesses all verified, of which 15 are over the real shipped functions and 1 is ORACLE VALIDATION, not actual-code verification: real_reference_decoder_agrees_with_core_str_len_le_3 (real.rs:104) ties the independent reference decoder in spec to core::str::from_utf8 and calls no ws_core function at all. It earns the reference decoder the right to be used as an oracle by the 15, which is why it is here, but counting it among harnesses 'over the real functions' overstated the actual-code figure by one. The harness's own doc comment always said ORACLE VALIDATION; this summary is what was wrong. 14 of 15 planted defects were detected, 1 was PROVEN EQUIVALENT, and 1 pair demonstrates a blind spot in a property this project already carries. The zero-dependency gate is untouched: rust/ still reports 0 non-path dependencies and ac1-gates is 8/8.

The view carries no `rust-version`, which is a cargo POLICY field with no effect on generated code, so the MSRV gate never fires for the verification pass while the shipped manifest and pin stay exactly as they are.

negative_control.discipline: Run and read BEFORE any positive claim. Each mutant is a defect-planted COPY of a target function; the SAME spec predicate is applied to the copy that the real harness applies to the shipped function. Every harness was run as its own process and its REAL exit status read (cmd: assurance/formal/kani/runner).

findings.title: M11 (control payload ceiling 125 -> 126) is an EQUIVALENT mutant, proven so
findings.detail: The mutant was planted expecting detection and Kani reported SUCCESS. The reason is sound and was then proven directly: decode_frame_header rejects a control frame carrying an extended-length marker (marker >= 126) BEFORE the ceiling check is reached, so the ceiling only ever sees payload_len == marker <= 125. Both `> 125` and `> 126` are dead comparisons for control frames. nc_m11_control_limit_proven_equivalent_to_clean_clone proves output-identity to the clean clone over all buffers of length <= 14 and all u64 caps. M15 (ceiling tightened to 124) was added as the REACHABLE control-ceiling mutant and IS detected.
findings.consequence: The control-ceiling dimension retains a live negative control. The port is not affected: this is a statement about the mutant, not a defect.

findings.title: The mask INVOLUTION property is blind to key misalignment
findings.detail: M9 (key rotated by one) and M10 (first byte skipped) are both real defects. Both are DETECTED by the exact mask equation out[i] == in[i] ^ key[i % 4], and both are PROVEN NOT DETECTABLE by the involution property (mask twice == identity): nc_m9/nc_m10_..._involution_expected_success both verify SUCCESSFUL. XOR with ANY fixed per-index key function is an involution, so involution alone cannot pin the key-to-byte alignment.
findings.cross_check: This is not a gap in the existing suite: the merged E1 property family `masking_equation_involution_and_chunked_equivalence` already carries `apply_mask vs a naive independent XOR model` alongside involution. The finding is that the exact-equation half is the load-bearing one and must not be dropped.

findings.title: CBMC cannot bound core::str's validator loop under a symbolic slice length
findings.detail: Harnesses that call String::from_utf8 with a SYMBOLIC-length slice fail with an unwinding assertion in core::str::validations::run_utf8_validation (`Not unwinding loop ... iteration 16`), still failing at --unwind 16 after 924s. Kani reported FAILED with failed_checks=0 / total_checks=0, i.e. it failed LOUDLY rather than silently claiming success. Fixing the slice length per harness (len_eq_0/1/2/3) bounds the loop while leaving every byte symbolic, and all four then verify in under a minute each. Coverage is identical to the symbolic-length form.
findings.correction_of_an_earlier_diagnosis: This lane first attributed a 12-minute stall on a UTF-8 harness to std's word-at-a-time fast path. That was WRONG: the cause was a missing #[kani::unwind] bound on the harness's own slice-iterator loop (CBMC was unwinding past iteration 616 over a <= 4 byte slice). Adding the bound cut the harness to 6.5s. The std cost above is a separate, real, and measured effect.

nonclaims: NOT UNIVERSAL PROOF. Every property except the u16 close-code harnesses is proven only up to its stated bound. A defect that first appears at a payload of 5 bytes, a close reason of 4 bytes, or a frame buffer of 15 bytes is outside what was checked.

NOT RUN IN THE US-007 SANDBOX. The owner decision asks for execution inside the accepted US-007 sandbox profile under a fresh attempt id. That was NOT done. protected/us007-sbx-launcher is hard-wired to the OTHER plane's repo and protected paths (/Users/mikelady/hq/repos/public/verified-java-websocket-port and .../verified-java-websocket-port/protected/...) and requires an owner ed25519 signing secret; using it would have meant writing the Codex plane, which this lane is forbidden to do. Everything here ran on the host in an isolated git worktree instead. The digest-verified-acquisition condition WAS met; the sandbox-execution condition was NOT.
THE CONNECTION STATE MACHINE WAS NOT ATTEMPTED, per the owner decision's scope.

scan_spans AND Opcode::from_wire WERE NOT VERIFIED DIRECTLY. Both are pub(crate), so an external harness crate cannot call them. Length decoding and opcode mapping are covered only as they surface through the public decode_frame_header.

THE VERIFIER'S OWN CORRECTNESS IS ASSUMED. Kani/CBMC soundness is not established here; the negative control establishes only that this configuration DETECTS the 14 reachable defects planted against these specs.

THE NIGHTLY TOOLCHAIN IS NOT INDEPENDENTLY DIGEST-QUALIFIED THE WAY THE KANI BUNDLE IS. rustup installed nightly-2025-11-21 against its own signed manifests; this lane recorded the resulting rustc/cargo binary digests after the fact but did not verify them against a published checksum, because rustup does not expose one per binary.

NO ORACLE COMPARISON AGAINST JAVA WAS PERFORMED BY THIS LANE. The specs are derived from the RFC, the recorded Java semantics, and core::str; Java fidelity continues to rest on the existing corpus and live-oracle evidence.

SPEC-CORRELATION RISK IS REDUCED, NOT ELIMINATED. The UTF-8 reference decoder is structurally different from the shipped DFA (it reconstructs code points and validates by range; the DFA uses per-byte continuation windows and never computes a code point) and is itself tied to core::str::from_utf8 at length <= 3. The close-code specs are stated as range facts rather than as the implementation's branch order. Neither device is a guarantee of independence.
